# Secrets Bridge

> Secrets Bridge adds access requests, approvals and audit to the secrets you keep in AWS Secrets Manager and HashiCorp Vault. Values stay in your provider.

Secrets Bridge is a secrets control plane. It adds access requests, approvals, RBAC, policy, audit and agent execution around the secrets a team already keeps in AWS Secrets Manager or HashiCorp Vault. It keeps requests, approvals and audit metadata; secret values stay in the provider, and the agent runs inside the team's infrastructure and only connects out. Azure Key Vault and GCP Secret Manager are on the roadmap. It is open source and pre-1.0: see Product status for what works today.

Every page below is also available as Markdown at the linked URL, and https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/llms-full.txt has all of them in one file.

## Start here

- [Home](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/index.md): Secrets Bridge adds access requests, approvals and audit around secrets you keep in AWS Secrets Manager and HashiCorp Vault. Values stay in your provider.

## Overview

- [Overview](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/index.md): How Secrets Bridge fits between developers, agents, and the actual secret providers, without ever holding raw values in the Control Plane.
- [Product status](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/product-status.md): What Secrets Bridge actually does today: implemented and QA-certified features, what's in progress, and what's on the roadmap. No overclaiming.
- [Architecture](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/architecture.md): Secrets Bridge architecture: control plane, outbound-only agent and providers, trust boundaries, the read, patch and discovery flows, and wire encryption.
- [Teams and section heads](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/teams-and-section-heads.md): Model an organisation as an N-level team tree in Secrets Bridge and scope RBAC role grants to a team, so a section head's access covers the whole subtree.
- [Threat model & hard rules](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/threat-model.md): The hard rules Secrets Bridge never breaks, how tests, schema triggers and CI enforce each one, the attacks it defends against and the gaps still open.
- [Glossary](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/glossary.md): Definitions of Secrets Bridge terms used in the docs and code: access request, agent, audit event, policy rule, secret wrap, single-shot and workflow.
- [FAQ](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/faq.md): Short answers about Secrets Bridge: whether it stores secret values, supported providers, the outbound agent, approvals, prod reveal, audit and MFA.

## Components

- [Components](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/index.md): Nine repositories, one product. What each repo holds, what it deliberately doesn't, and the one-way dependency graph that keeps the agent infra-free.
- [Control Plane API](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/api.md): The Secrets Bridge control plane API in Go and Fiber v3: package layout, session-cookie identity, permission guards, runtime endpoints and configuration.
- [Agent](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/agent.md): The outbound-only Secrets Bridge agent inside your boundary: CI-enforced rules, enrollment at boot, configuration, executors and Vault and AWS resolvers.
- [Worker](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/worker.md): The Secrets Bridge worker: sweepers for expired wraps, stale agents, stuck jobs and Gateway tasks, Redis locks for multiple replicas, and webhook sinks.
- [Controller (Kubernetes)](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/controller.md): The Secrets Bridge Kubernetes controller: a SecretsSync CRD reconciler that validates provider refs and leaves sync work to the agent via the job queue.
- [Gateway](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/gateway.md): The optional Gateway runs in your boundary, reads Argo CD rollout state with GET-only calls and reports it as metadata. Release 1 scope and security model.
- [UI (SPA)](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/ui.md): The Secrets Bridge console: a React and TypeScript SPA for access requests, one-time reveals, agents, audit and admin, and nothing in browser storage.
- [Core (shared library)](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/core.md): The infra-free Go library behind Secrets Bridge services: the Provider interface with its metadata and value split, Vault and AWS connectors and redaction.

## Operations

- [Operations](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/index.md): Run Secrets Bridge in production: install the Helm charts from GHCR, what you provide around them, and the hardening checklist before you expose it.
- [Running locally with docker compose](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/docker-compose.md): Run Secrets Bridge on your laptop with docker compose: Postgres and Redis, the api and UI, and an agent enrolled against a HashiCorp Vault dev server.
- [Bootstrap & first sign-in](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/bootstrap.md): First steps on a new Secrets Bridge install: seed the local admin, sign in, rotate its password, enroll an agent with a one-time token, run a read request.
- [Agent onboarding](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/agent-onboarding.md): How a Secrets Bridge agent enrolls with a one-time token, gets a persistent identity once, heartbeats outbound and can be revoked. No inbound ports needed.
- [Authentication](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/authentication.md): How Secrets Bridge signs users in: cookie-only sessions, account lockout, OIDC with group-to-role mapping, MFA step-up with TOTP or WebAuthn, break-glass.
- [Sign in with Google](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/google-sign-in.md): Connect a Google Workspace to Secrets Bridge from the console, approve the accounts it creates and link Google to existing accounts. Not yet through QA.
- [OIDC with Authentik](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/oidc-authentik.md): Set up Authentik as the OIDC provider for Secrets Bridge, step by step: the application, scopes, group claim, MFA, step-up and back-channel logout.
- [Project environments](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/project-environments.md): Project environments in Secrets Bridge: the non_prod and prod kind that gates direct reveal, why it is separate from type, the backfill rule and the API.
- [Policy templates](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/policy-templates.md): Copy-paste Secrets Bridge policy rules: non-prod direct reveal, prod single and multi-approver workflows, cross-team templates and scoped policy authoring.
- [Reveal sessions](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/reveal-sessions.md): How Secrets Bridge reveal sessions work: a time-limited window to view approved secret values, the policy-driven TTL, the hard rules and operator queries.
- [Cross-team requests](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/cross-team-requests.md): Cross-team requests in Secrets Bridge: one team fills a value another team needs, with separation of duties, approval, a state machine and triage SQL.
- [Provider connections](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/provider-connections.md): Register HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager as a provider connection, bind it to projects and environments, and run discovery. It holds no credentials.
- [Gateway](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/gateway.md): Install a Release 1 Gateway for Argo CD observation: a read-only Argo CD account, one-time enrollment, the Helm chart, connector approval and bindings.
- [Gateway cutover](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/gateway-cutover.md): Move an install from the retired control-plane Argo CD poller to Gateway observation: bind Gateways first, upgrade, rotate the Argo CD token, clean up.
- [Object storage](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/object-storage.md): Store media such as project and team logos in AWS S3 or an S3-compatible server. Covers IAM, encryption, bucket settings, backups and the logo migration.
- [Verifying images and charts](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/verifying-releases.md): Check the cosign signature, SBOM and build provenance of Secrets Bridge container images and Helm charts before you deploy them.
- [Configuration reference](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/config.md): Every Secrets Bridge environment variable for the api, agent, worker, controller and Gateway, with defaults, retired settings and insecure dev switches.
- [Troubleshooting](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/troubleshooting.md): Fix common Secrets Bridge problems: login 401s, Google sign-in, failed agent jobs, stale agents, Vault permission errors, Gateway issues and audit queries.

## Reference

- [Reference](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/reference/index.md): Reference pages for Secrets Bridge: every HTTP API endpoint, the supported secret providers, the KMS backends and the RBAC permission catalog.
- [HTTP API endpoints](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/reference/api-endpoints.md): Every HTTP endpoint the Secrets Bridge api exposes and its auth gate: sign-in, agents, Gateways, access requests, reveal sessions, audit and policy rules.
- [Providers supported](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/reference/providers.md): Secret providers the Secrets Bridge agent supports: HashiCorp Vault KV v2 and AWS Secrets Manager, with auth and config. Azure and GCP are on the roadmap.
- [KMS backends](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/reference/kms-backends.md): The KMS backends Secrets Bridge uses for envelope encryption: local for dev only, HashiCorp Vault Transit and AWS KMS for production, setup and rotation.
- [Permissions catalog](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/reference/permissions.md): The Secrets Bridge RBAC permission catalog: the seed roles, every permission string checked by auth.Require, scoped grants and how to add a permission.

## Optional

- [Design system](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/design/index.md): The Secrets Bridge design system: brand voice, colour and type tokens, and the logos and assets shared by the console, this site and the brand marks.
- [Brand voice](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/design/brand-voice.md): How Secrets Bridge describes itself: say what we keep, describe the mechanism and label maturity exactly, with examples and the words we avoid.
- [Tokens and theme](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/design/tokens.md): Secrets Bridge design tokens: colours for the light and dark themes, the type scale, spacing, radii and control sizes used by the console and this site.
- [Logos and assets](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/design/assets.md): The Secrets Bridge Checkpoint mark, its lockups and approved colourings, the four product icons and the architecture illustration.
